we can now see the neural network as a complex dynamical system, in which different time scales are interacting, and that the dynamics of the system can be studied by the methods of nonlinear dynamics and statistical mechanics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
precise joint-spiking activity can occur in cortical networks, even if the neurons are not strongly connected.
the brain can perform computations with millisecond time scales, and that this can be achieved by using a combination of precise joint spikes and precise temporal coding.
, in the brain, the precise temporal organization of neural activity may play a role that is at least as important as the precise timing of single spikes.
